title: Kanagawa University's fourth report: MNS account data on its authentication platform may have leaked
summary: Cybersecurity.com (Japan) reports that Kanagawa University published a fourth report on unauthorized access to its authentication platform. According to the report, MNS account names, IDs, passwords and email addresses may have leaked, while JINDAI account passwords did not leak because it is a separate system. The university says no secondary damage has been confirmed and asks users to change passwords. The number affected was not given.
plain: Kanagawa University says login data for its MNS accounts may have leaked after unauthorized access. It has asked users to change their passwords and says no secondary damage has been confirmed.
exec: A university reports that account credentials on its authentication platform may have leaked; it gave no number of people affected.
action: Kanagawa University asks users to change their passwords promptly and to change them on any other sites where the same password was used.
